title: Issue #178: catalog: define X33 event governance, messaging and distributed workflow contracts
content:
State: open

## X33 – Ecosystem Event Governance, Messaging & Distributed Workflow Coordination

**Architecture-ID:** `ATC-CROSSCUTTING-X33-EVENT-GOVERNANCE-MESSAGING-DISTRIBUTED-WORKFLOW-COORDINATION`  
**Status:** `PROPOSED / NOT VERIFIED`  
**Planned scope:** 17 sublayers · 170 planned function contracts  
**Systems:** A‑TownChain, GlobusOS, ShivaCore, Aurora AI

## Goal and scope

Define cross-cutting governance contracts for events, messages, and distributed workflows so components communicate through explicit interfaces, event processing is traceable, and failures, retries, replays, or partial outages do not cause uncontrolled side effects.

X33 defines architecture and function contracts only. It must **not** introduce its own message broker, global event bus, workflow executor, workflow engine, or blockchain mechanism.

### Boundaries

- **X3 – Protocol & Interoperability:** protocol and interoperability foundations.
- **X7 – Observability, Reliability & Resilience:** operational observability and resilience.
- **X18 – Ecosystem Integrity & Catalog Drift:** architecture and catalog consistency.
- **X32 – API Security & Zero-Trust Integration:** authentication, authorization, and secure API mediation.
- **X33:** event semantics, delivery guarantees, ordering, retries, workflow states, and cross-system coordination.

## 17 sublayers / 170 planned contracts

The contracts below are planned—not evidence that functions already exist, are cataloged, or are implemented. Each sublayer contains 10 planned contracts, with the stable ID ranges shown.

| Sublayer | Scope | Planned IDs |
|---|---|---|
| X33.01 – Event Taxonomy & Canonical Event Schema | Canonical event types and IDs; schema versions and compatibility; required/optional fields; producer, source, event/recorded times, correlation/causation, classification; unknown-schema handling | X33-001–010 |
| X33.02 – Event Production & Publication Governance | Producer registration and authorization; validation; approved channels; publication outcomes and failures; duplicate publication; payload limits and data minimization; unpublished-event traceability | X33-011–020 |
| X33.03 – Message Routing & Channel Governance | Channel registry; routing rules and versions; authorized recipients/capabilities; unknown destinations fail-closed; cycle limits; priority; channel retirement/migration; auditable routing decisions | X33-021–030 |
| X33.04 – Delivery Semantics & Acknowledgement | Explicit delivery guarantees; standardized acknowledgements; receive vs. process acknowledgement; attempt IDs, deadlines, unacknowledged messages, persistent status, unreachable-recipient classification, documented guarantee limits | X33-031–040 |
| X33.05 – Ordering, Sequencing & Causal Consistency | Per-channel ordering requirements; sequence validation and gaps; per-aggregate order; causal references; late events; constrained parallelism; concurrent-event conflicts; timestamps are not proof of causality | X33-041–050 |
| X33.06 – Idempotency, Deduplication & Replay Protection | Idempotency keys; processed-message detection; persistent deduplication; duplicate side-effect prevention; replay windows/retention; replay vs. legitimate retry; external API limits; safe dedup failures; workflow restart; audit | X33-051–060 |
| X33.07 – Retry, Backoff & Dead-Letter Governance | Retry policy; exponential backoff/jitter; retry budgets; transient/permanent error classification; dead-letter channels; cause archival; authorized redrive; side-effect checks; retry-storm limits; escalation | X33-061–070 |
| X33.08 – Event Persistence, Outbox & Inbox | Persistence requirements; transactional outbox; inbox state; state-change/publication coordination; incomplete publication detection; persistence guarantees; retention, deletion/archive traceability, checkpoints, explicit data-loss errors | X33-071–080 |
| X33.09 – Workflow Definition & State Machine Contracts | Workflow registry; states/transitions and guards; terminal/cancel states; immutable workflow versions; invalid-transition rejection; unique instances; event-linked transitions; timeouts/runtime limits; invariant checks | X33-081–090 |
| X33.10 – Distributed Transactions & Saga Coordination | Saga modeling; local transaction boundaries; compensation registration/order; non-compensable actions; partial/intermediate states; no assumed distributed atomicity; conflict escalation; approved manual intervention; auditable outcomes | X33-091–100 |
| X33.11 – Backpressure, Flow Control & Load Shedding | Queue/buffer bounds; producer throttling; consumer capacity; standard backpressure; overload rejection classification; prioritized load shedding; no unbounded queues; workflow budgets; controlled recovery; telemetry links | X33-101–110 |
| X33.12 – Event Replay, Recovery & Reconciliation | Replayable ranges and positions; isolated replay runs; historical vs. live processing; deterministic reconstruction; prevent/simulate external side effects; checkpoint validation; source/target reconciliation; discrepancy classification; measurable recovery completion | X33-111–120 |
| X33.13 – Cross-Service Orchestration & Dependency Governance | Service dependencies; workflow-to-service contracts; cycle detection; readiness/start conditions; timeouts; failure domains/isolation; capability checks; version conflicts; degraded availability; architecture-graph evidence | X33-121–130 |
| X33.14 – Event Security, Integrity & Trust Boundaries | Origin/trust validation; integrity protection; producer/consumer permission separation; schema/size attack validation; data minimization; conditional signatures; quarantine untrusted events; protect sensitive transitions; record tampering; cross-boundary policy | X33-131–140 |
| X33.15 – Auditability, Correlation & Distributed Tracing | Trace/correlation IDs; cross-service event chains; workflow-to-run/span references; audit vs. debug logs; tamper protection; clock skew/missing telemetry; sensitive-data redaction; cause correlation; audit access/retention; completeness evidence | X33-141–150 |
| X33.16 – Blockchain, GlobusOS & Aurora Event Adapters | Canonical blockchain-event integration; block height/transaction/finality distinction; provisional non-final events; reorgs/revocation; approved GlobusOS interfaces; Aurora policy/capability checks; approval pauses; untrusted external model/API results; no duplicate implementations; adapter provenance/conformance | X33-151–160 |
| X33.17 – Conformance, Testing & Lifecycle Governance | Conformance tests; schema compatibility; duplicate/delay/out-of-order simulation; crash/recovery tests; idempotency/compensation evidence; load/backpressure/queue bounds; security/authorization tests; Run/Job/Step evidence; catalog statuses/source refs; versioned retirement/migration | X33-161–170 |

**Contract completeness requirement:** Expand every planned ID into an individual catalog record with stable ID, contract semantics, owner, canonical repository/path/symbol, status, tests, and evidence. The ID ranges above are a planning index, not a claim that all 170 descriptions have already been reconciled with the live catalog.

## Proposed event envelope: `ATC-EVENT-CONTRACT-V1`

This YAML is a proposal, not a normative `atc-standards` registry entry. `required`, `conditional`, and rule values are placeholders until types, serialization, cryptographic bindings, and normative error codes are specified.

```yaml
contract_id: ATC-EVENT-CONTRACT-V1
schema_version: 1
event:
  event_id: required
  event_type: required
  occurred_at: required
  recorded_at: required
  producer_id: required
  correlation_id: required
  causation_id: optional
  aggregate_id: optional
  sequence_number: conditional
  classification: required
  payload_schema: required
  payload: required
delivery:
  channel_id: required
  delivery_semantics: explicitly_declared
  idempotency_key: required_for_side_effects
  expires_at: optional
  retry_policy_ref: required
workflow:
  workflow_id: optional
  workflow_version: optional
  workflow_state: optional
  approval_ref: conditional
security:
  producer_identity: required
  authorization_context: required
  integrity_proof: conditional
provenance:
  source_repository: conditional
  source_commit_sha: conditional
  source_path: conditional
  evidence_ref: conditional
rules:
  unknown_schema: reject_or_quarantine
  unauthorized_producer: reject
  duplicate_processing: idempotent_or_reject
  unfinalized_blockchain_event: provisional
  missing_required_evidence: not_verified
```

## SSOT and implementation boundaries

- `a-townchain-ecosystem`: cross-cutting architecture, catalog mappings, integration/compliance/evidence/drift only; no duplicate production implementation.
- `atc-standards`: normative event schemas and protocol rules only after formal registration/versioning.
- `a-townchain`: canonical blockchain core, transaction state, and blockchain events.
- `a-townchain/components/vm`: canonical ATC-VM execution/events.
- `a-townchain/components/algorithm`: canonical algorithm/consensus events.
- `globus-os/modules/atc-shivacore/kernel/`: canonical ShivaCore kernel/system events.
- `globus-os`: desktop, OS services, and window/system events according to verified module boundaries.
- Aurora agents/runtime: verify canonical repository and source path before catalog mapping.
- Broker, event bus, persistence, workflow engine: inventory existing implementations and their SSOT first; do not assume or create a new global implementation.

If a suitable implementation is not found, record the gap as `UNRESOLVED` and assign it to a canonical repository before implementation.

## Mandatory architecture invariants

1. **Standalone First, Ecosystem Second:** components own their local contracts; the ecosystem coordinates integration and conformance.
2. No implicit delivery guarantees. Never claim “exactly once” without precise semantics and evidence; combine at-least-once delivery with deduplication/idempotent processing where appropriate.
3. No silent loss: rejections, dead letters, persistence failures, and unresolved workflows must be visible and classified.
4. Retries, replay, and recovery must not cause unintended duplicate external side effects.
5. Fail closed at security-critical boundaries: missing identity, authorization, or required approval means rejection or quarantine.
6. Blockchain events are not automatically final; chain-specific finality and reorganization rules govern.
7. Timestamps alone do not prove global ordering or causality.
8. Catalog contracts do not replace canonical production code.
9. `IMPLEMENTED` requires source evidence; `VERIFIED` requires reproducible tests and appropriate runtime evidence.
10. Never invent source references: repository, full 40-character commit SHA, path, symbol, blob SHA, workflow Run/Job/Step, exit code/logs, and artifact hashes must be grounded in actual evidence. Unknowns remain `UNRESOLVED`.

## Implementation sequence

1. Inventory existing event, messaging, workflow components and dependencies; separate existing implementation from planned contracts.
2. Specify canonical event schema/versioning, identity, routing, and error semantics; document format conflicts.
3. Test idempotency, deduplication, retry, outbox/inbox, replay, and dead-letter/recovery behavior.
4. Specify state machines, timeouts, saga compensation, and approval boundaries; implement only in the canonical repository.
5. Integrate blockchain, GlobusOS, and Aurora using verified interfaces; test finality, capabilities, and external side effects separately.
6. Archive test results, immutable artifact hashes, full commit SHAs, and complete workflow evidence before changing statuses.

## Readiness checklist (0/12)

- [ ] Inventory existing event and messaging implementations.
- [ ] Establish SSOT and source path per component/function group.
- [ ] Compare all 17 sublayers and 170 planned contracts against the live catalog.
- [ ] Normatively specify event schema and versioning.
- [ ] Define delivery, ordering, and idempotency guarantees precisely.
- [ ] Test retry, dead-letter, replay, and recovery.
- [ ] Specify workflow state machines and compensations.
- [ ] Review zero-trust and approval boundaries.
- [ ] Test blockchain finality and reorganization behavior.
- [ ] Archive conformance runs with Run/Job/Step evidence.
- [ ] Record full SHAs, paths, symbols, and artifact hashes.
- [ ] Classify each contract using evidence-based statuses.

Checking a box is not proof of implementation or verification.

## Acceptance criteria

- Catalog all 17 sublayers and reconcile all 170 IDs against existing entries without duplicates.
- Each contract has an owner, exact canonical source reference or documented `UNRESOLVED` status, semantics, negative/failure tests, and evidence.
- No new global event bus/broker/workflow engine is introduced by this architecture issue.
- Delivery/retry/replay/ordering guarantees and side-effect boundaries are explicit and tested.
- Security, approvals, blockchain finality/reorgs, recovery, and audit requirements have negative-path tests.
- CI evidence includes exact full commit SHA and Run → Job → Step, exit code/logs, and hashed artifacts.
- Statuses are assigned only with evidence: `MAPPED`, `IMPLEMENTED`, `VERIFIED`, `RESIDUAL`, `BLOCKED`, `EXCLUDED`, or `UNRESOLVED`.

## Current status

- Architecture design: `PROPOSED`
- Catalog intake: `NOT VERIFIED`
- Production implementation: `UNRESOLVED`
- Planned sublayers: 17
- Planned function contracts: 170

**Next required step:** compare X33 with the existing ecosystem catalog and actual repository implementations. Issue creation or catalog planning alone does not establish a commit, implementation, or successful CI verification.

The live drift gate must continue to exclude `demo-repository`.
